finding.claim: _get_regex_literal escapes only ' \b \f \n \r \t and not backslash or NUL. A literal backspace in a JSON Schema pattern becomes the two-character \b inside a raw string, which regex reads as a word boundary, so generated constr(pattern=...) validation accepts different strings than the schema specifies. A NUL byte is not escaped and can make ast.literal_eval raise ValueError (not SyntaxError) on Python <3.12, crashing generation. No code injection: literal_eval requires a single complete literal and the fallback is repr-rendered.
finding.source: JSON Schema 'pattern' string supplied in the input schema
finding.sink: PythonCode raw literal emitted into generated constr(pattern=...) validation code

trace.note: escape_characters table omits backslash and NUL

finding.guards_checked: ast.literal_eval validates a single complete string literal, which rules out code injection. SyntaxError fallback returns a plain str rendered via repr. Not executed: Bash was disabled, so the mismatch and NUL behavior are from reading the code.

finding.claim: Relative $ref file paths are joined to the schema base directory and resolved without a containment check, so '../' refs can point outside the schema directory. The loader then reads the resolved file. Contents leak only if they reach generated output or error messages. Absolute path-style refs are confined; relative refs are not.
